front: Which Anglo-Saxon monastery became a mission base for converting the northern kingdoms?
note: English Heritage, “Significance of Lindisfarne Priory,” lines 227–234: the monastery founded in 635 became a base for converting northern Anglo-Saxon kingdoms from paganism to Christianity.

front: What feudal service did vavassors of Mont-Saint-Michel owe after its property acquisition around 1024?
note: David Crouch, “Military Service in Normandy Before 1066,” Anglo-Norman Studies V, Cambridge University Press, lines 466 onward. The passage discusses military service owed by vavassors to Mont-Saint-Michel after it acquired properties around 1024. It cautions that the claim that the duke had imposed the whole obligation earlier relies on later evidence; the card tests the attested service only.

front: How did Domesday commissioners verify local evidence?
note: Herefordshire Through Time, “How was the Domesday Book created?,” lines 41–50: commissioners took evidence on oath, used local juries to verify facts, and collated the information.

front: Which town did Swein Forkbeard’s army storm in 1003?
note: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, annals 1003–1004, lines 2260–2275: Exeter was entered by storm in 1003, the army then moved into Wiltshire, and Sweyn led it to Milton; the following year he led the force to Norwich.

front: Which earldom did Cnut assign to Thorkell in the 1017 division of England?
note: Ryan Lavelle, “Cnut, King of the English, 1017–19,” University of Winchester, lines 7–10: in the 1017 division of England, East Anglia went to Thorkell.

front: Which court did Hitler create in Berlin in 1934 for treason and major political cases?
note: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, “Law and Justice in the Third Reich,” lines 135–136: Hitler created special courts in 1933 and the People’s Court in Berlin in 1934 to hear treason and major political cases.

front: Which farming practice was central to early Norse Greenland settlements?
note: “Cultural Adaptation, Compounding Vulnerabilities and Conjunctures in Norse Greenland,” PNAS, lines 157–158: pastoralism and livestock grazing strongly conditioned Norse settlement in Greenland; livestock production was supplemented by wild resources.

front: According to a 1935 Social Democratic report from Lübeck, how did some viewers respond to Triumph of the Will?
note: USHMM, “The Weapons of Dictatorship: Terror and Propaganda,” lines 129–131: a June 1935 underground German Social Democratic Party public-opinion report from Lübeck says Nazi films such as Triumph of the Will were avoided.
